findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, so the database receives a public IP/DNS name reachable from the internet rather than being confined to the VPC. Combined with the inbound rule permitting MySQL from the whole VPC CIDR and an app instance whose public DNS is exported, this materially increases the exposure of a directly internet-addressable database.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the MySQL database data, backups, and snapshots unencrypted on disk, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the catalog data.

The DB password is interpolated from var.password into the EC2 user_data bootstrap script and written in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. Instance user data and the resulting web-accessible include file disclose the database admin credentials to anyone who can read them through instance metadata or HTTP.

The master username is the fixed, well-known value 'admin', and the same password is used by the web application. A predictable admin account name lowers the effort required for credential-stuffing or brute-force attempts against the exposed database.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*" to the catalog application role. Any compromise of the app server, which also runs a public-facing PHP application, yields full control of S3, EC2, and RDS across the account, including the ability to exfiltrate data and escalate privileges.

The database security group allows all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0, removing any egress containment and enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from the database if it is ever compromised.

The inbound rule allows MySQL from the entire VPC CIDR block, so any instance in the VPC — including the apparently compromised or misconfigured app server with * permissions — can reach the database, defeating least-privilege network segmentation.

The configuration exports the application instance's public DNS name, indicating the app server is directly reachable from the internet. This places the PHP application that embeds the database admin password behind a public network endpoint.
backup_retention_period = 0 with skip_final_snapshot = true means no automated backups are retained, weakening the ability to recover the database after destructive tampering.
